column1: Single-seed (seed=42) ablation run and its McNemar test were found to be non-reproducible because the original ablation training loop did not fix a random seed; repeated execution produced different weight initialization and data shuffling, yielding inconsistent metrics across runs. These single-seed results are therefore excluded from the paper's primary evidence. The multi-seed (42, 123, 2024) repeated-measures ANOVA, which used explicit seed control, is reproducible and is used as the primary statistical evidence (p=0.988 accuracy, p=0.985 F1 — no significant architecture effect).
